Heard Sri Sunil Srivastava, learned counsel for the applicants and Sri U.P. Singh, learned counsel for the State and perused the record.

This application under Section 482 Cr.P.C. has been filed by the applicants Akbar Abbass Zaidi,
Asgar Abbass, Mudasir and Danish Raza with the prayer to allow the present application and quash the order dated 30.01.2023, F.R. No. 969/12 of 2022 (Nasir Vs. Akbar Abbass Zaidi and others) in Case Crime No. 556 of 2021, under Sections 420, 467, 471, 120-B I.P.C., Police Station Kairana,
District Shamli, pending before Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Kairana, Shamli and with a further prayer to stay the order dated 30.01.2023 of the aforesaid case, during the pendency of the present application.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicants at the very outset argued that the order impugned dated 30.01.2023 directing further investigation and submitting a report thereupon passed by the Chief Judicial Magistrate, Kairana is bad in the eyes of law and abuse of process of court, inasmuch as, the matter has previously been investigated and a final report was submitted but even thereafter on the protest petition, the trial court has passed the said order.
It is argued that there is no occasion for the trial court to pass the said order as the matter is a civil dispute and there was nothing remaining for investigation.

Learned counsel has further argued that even the Circle Officer, Kairana, District Shamli has given a report dated 04.04.2021 to the effect that no matter is there for investigation and as such the trial court should have considered the same and dropped the proceedings and accepted the final report.
It is further argued that there are civil litigation pending between the parties and even there is an order in favour of the applicant passed by the civil court which is still in operation.

It is argued that as such directing the matter again for further investigation would not be in the fitness of things and would not end the dispute but would keep it pending and the investigation would go on which would prejudice the applicant.
The complainant has filed protest petition with malafide intentions which is clearly abuse of process of law.
It is argued that the dispute between the parties is only with regards to a single document dated 26.01.2019 titled as a Yaddast Tehrir/Raseed.
It is argued that as such the order dated 30.01.2023 be set aside and the matter was directed to be closed by the trial court and no further investigation is needed.

Per contra, learned counsel for the State opposed the prayer for quashing and argued that the protest petition was filed by the opposite party no.2 after investigation on which the trial court after going through the matter came to the conclusion that further investigation was required and as such directed to be investigated further and a report after it be submitted.
It is argued that the said order has not in any manner prejudiced the applicant, inasmuch as, only further investigation has been ordered.
It is argued that the present petition does not call for any interference as the applicant is not at all aggrieved by the said order for further investigation.

After having heard learned counsel for the parties and perusing the records, it is evident that the protest petition filed by the complainant was considered by the trial court after which on 20.01.2023, the final report no. 67 of 2021 was rejected and the matter was referred for further investigation.
The Investigating Agency was directed to file its report to the court concerned.
The said order is a detailed order on merits by merely sending for further investigation.
The applicant cannot have any grievance.
It is expected always that the investigation is done fairly and impartially after which the trial court would apply its judicial mind and proceeded with it.
In view of the same, no case for interference is made out.
The present application under Section 482 Cr.P.C. is thus rejected.
